newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UNILEVER SET FOR SUBDUED Q1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UNILEVER SET FOR SUBDUED Q1.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch foods and consumer products group Unilever Plc/NV is likely to adopt a low key approach to its first quarter results on Friday in view of a weaker trading environment, said analysts.
Brokers are also expecting a below trend performance, partly because an early Easter cut two trading days off the quarter.
"The trading environment everywhere, if anything, is worse which means the company is likely to give a cautious tone to its results," said Paribas analyst John Campbell.

Analysts forecasts range from 530-585 million stg, up from 509 million last time. Many also expect Unilever executives to be downbeat in their comments in an effort to take some of the froth off its share price.
"I think Unilever is getting nervous about the share price and the expectations building up in the market," said Lehman Brothers analyst Richard Newboult.

Unilever shares, currently trading at 1612p have set a high of 1662p and a low of 1073p so far this year, surging ahead since it announced plans to sell its speciality chemicals division on February 11.
The share price has benefited in part from heavy buying by U.S. funds of Unilever NV.

Two other distortions are also likely to hit this year's figures. There should be a 25 million stg benefit from the company's pension fund holiday. Also, last year the company provided 15 million stg to write off its stock of beef for Walls' burgers.

Unilever's mainland European business is expected to reflect continued weakness in trading, with Germany flat to lower, Italy becoming weaker and France getting worse. Analysts also expect North American operations to show signs of a slowdown.
